claims.text: The framework for uncertainty estimation is based on Bayesian belief networks and Monte-Carlo sampling.
The framework incorporates prior data information such as sensor noise.
The framework is agnostic to the network architecture and task.
The framework does not require changes in the optimization process.
The framework can be applied to already trained architectures.
The proposed framework outperforms previous methods by up to 23% in accuracy on computer vision and control tasks.

evidence.description: We thoroughly validate the proposed framework through extensive experiments on both computer vision and control tasks, where we outperform previous methods by up to 23% in accuracy.

methodologies.name: Bayesian belief network and Monte-Carlo sampling uncertainty framework
methodologies.description: A general architecture-agnostic framework for uncertainty estimation modeling different prediction uncertainty sources and integrating prior data information.

limitations.text: Current approaches for uncertainty estimation of neural networks require changes to the network and optimization process.
Current approaches typically ignore prior knowledge about the data.
Current approaches tend to make over-simplifying assumptions which underestimate uncertainty.
